Merge two tables with a Stata-style match report

Source: R/merge.R
stata_merge.Rd

stata_merge() joins using onto .data like Stata's merge. It checks the stated key relationship first, keeps master, using and matched rows by default, reports how many rows fell into each group, and records the result in a .merge column (Stata's _merge).

Usage

stata_merge(
  .data,
  using,
  relationship,
  by,
  keep = c("master", "using", "match"),
  assert = NULL,
  generate = ".merge",
  report = TRUE
)

Arguments

.data

The master table: a data frame, tibble, or data.table.

using

The table to merge in.

relationship

The key relationship, as in Stata: "1:1" (keys unique in both tables), "m:1" (unique in using) or "1:m" (unique in .data). It is required and checked before joining. Stata's many-to-many (m:m) merge is not supported. Use dplyr::inner_join() with relationship = "many-to-many" if you need all pairings.

by

A character vector of key columns. Use a named vector, such as c(id = "person_id"), when the names differ (.data name = using name).

keep

Which rows to keep: any of "master" (only in .data), "using" (only in using) and "match" (in both). Default keeps all, as Stata does.

assert

NULL (default) or any of "master", "using" and "match". If given, every row must be in one of these groups, otherwise stata_merge() errors, like Stata's assert() option.

generate

Name of the result column, ".merge" by default. Use NULL to omit it (Stata's nogenerate).

report

If TRUE (default), print the match report as a message.

Value

An ungrouped merged table in the data.frame, tibble, or data.table container of .data. Retained rows from .data come first in their original order, followed by rows found only in using. Unless generate = NULL, the match-status column (.merge by default) is a factor with levels "master only", "using only", and "matched".

Details

Missing key values match each other, as in Stata. When a non-key column exists in both tables, matched rows keep the values from .data, including missing values, as Stata does without update. Rows found only in using keep its values. Shared columns use a compatible common type when using-only values are needed; incompatible types cause an error. A message identifies shared columns; rename them first to keep both. Grouping is not retained.

See also

Other data checking functions: assert(), is_first(), keys

Examples

people <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, age = c(30, 41, 25))
income <- tibble::tibble(id = c(2, 3, 4), income = c(10, 20, 30))
stata_merge(people, income, "1:1", by = "id")
#> Result                            Rows
#> --------------------------------------
#> Not matched                          2
#>     from master                      1  (.merge == "master only")
#>     from using                       1  (.merge == "using only")
#> 
#> Matched                              2  (.merge == "matched")
#> --------------------------------------
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>      id   age income .merge     
#>   <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <fct>      
#> 1     1    30     NA master only
#> 2     2    41     10 matched    
#> 3     3    25     20 matched    
#> 4     4    NA     30 using only 

# Require every person to be matched
try(stata_merge(people, income, "1:1", by = "id", assert = "match"))
#> Result                            Rows
#> --------------------------------------
#> Not matched                          2
#>     from master                      1  (.merge == "master only")
#>     from using                       1  (.merge == "using only")
#> 
#> Matched                              2  (.merge == "matched")
#> --------------------------------------
#> Error in stata_merge(people, income, "1:1", by = "id", assert = "match") : 
#>   Merge assertion failed: found 1 master only row(s) and 1 using only
#> row(s); `assert` allows only matched.

# Keep matched rows only
stata_merge(people, income, "1:1", by = "id", keep = "match", report = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>      id   age income .merge 
#>   <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <fct>  
#> 1     2    41     10 matched
#> 2     3    25     20 matched

# Many people per household
members <- tibble::tibble(hh = c(1, 1, 2), person = 1:3)
households <- tibble::tibble(hh = 1:2, region = c("north", "south"))
stata_merge(members, households, "m:1", by = "hh")
#> Result                            Rows
#> --------------------------------------
#> Not matched                          0
#>     from master                      0  (.merge == "master only")
#>     from using                       0  (.merge == "using only")
#> 
#> Matched                              3  (.merge == "matched")
#> --------------------------------------
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>      hh person region .merge 
#>   <dbl>  <int> <chr>  <fct>  
#> 1     1      1 north  matched
#> 2     1      2 north  matched
#> 3     2      3 south  matched
